gold_patch_assessment: The gold patch comprehensively addresses the full issue: it introduces DmenuProvider (new files dmenu_provider.cpp/h), adds DmenuEntryConfig and LauncherConfig to config_types.h, wires up the schema in config_schema.cpp, registers/reloads providers in application.cpp, moves launcher settings from shell.panel to shell.launcher across session_provider, launcher_panel, and settings_registry, and updates meson.build. The implementation is thorough and correct for the stated requirements.
base_vs_gold_expectation: The base repo will be rejected: applying the test patch changes the roundtrip test to reference c.shell.launcher.compact (etc.) which does not exist in the base config_types.h, so compilation will fail. The gold-patched repo will pass: the test patch references fields that the gold patch creates in ShellConfig::LauncherConfig, and the roundtrip test will succeed. So the verifier correctly discriminates base from gold.
too_narrow_risks: The test only verifies the config migration (moving 3 launcher booleans from shell.panel to shell.launcher). It does not test any aspect of the DmenuProvider feature, which is the primary subject of the issue.

The test binary (config_schema_roundtrip_test) is compiled from a standalone source list that does NOT include dmenu_provider.cpp, launcher_panel.cpp, application.cpp, or session_provider.cpp. A candidate that only restructures config_types.h and config_schema.cpp would pass without implementing DmenuProvider at all.
No test verifies DmenuEntryConfig parsing from TOML (the [shell.launcher.dmenu.entry.<id>] tables).
No test verifies dmenu command execution, tab-delimited line splitting, fuzzy filtering, result capping, timeout/size limits, exec template substitution, or clipboard fallback.
No test verifies clearProvidersWithIdPrefix, reloadDmenuProviders, or the config reload callback.
The test patch changes only 3 lines and adds zero new assertions. It tests exactly one pre-existing test (config schema roundtrip) with field name adjustments.
A partial implementation (config struct changes only, no DmenuProvider, no application wiring, no launcher_panel changes) would pass.
implementation_coupling: The test is not coupled to the gold implementation's internals — it tests observable config roundtrip behavior. However, it is coupled to the specific field naming convention (shell.launcher.compact vs shell.launcher.launcherCompact, etc.), which is reasonable since these are the schema field names.
environment_risks: The eval script uses 'meson setup build-debug --reconfigure' which should handle stale build state, and the Docker image pre-configures the build directory. Build tool availability (meson 1.3.2, ninja 1.11.1) is confirmed in the image.
No network, external data, or timing dependencies in the test.
mismatches: Major scope mismatch: the issue describes a comprehensive DmenuProvider feature (command execution, line parsing, fuzzy filtering, activation, config-driven registration, lazy loading) plus a config migration. The test only validates the config migration portion, leaving the entire DmenuProvider feature untested.
The task.toml categorizes this as 'debugging' but it is clearly a new feature implementation with config refactoring.

evidence.detail: Test patch only changes 3 lines in config_schema_roundtrip_test.cpp: s/shell.panel.launcherCompact/shell.launcher.compact/ and similar for sessionSearch and sortByUsage. Zero dmenu-related assertions.
The config_schema_roundtrip_test executable compiles only config/schema/theme sources. It does NOT compile or link dmenu_provider.cpp, launcher_panel.cpp, application.cpp, or session_provider.cpp.
Eval compiles only the config_schema_roundtrip_test target, not the full application. DmenuProvider code is never built or tested by the verifier.
Issue describes DmenuProvider as the primary feature. Config migration is a secondary 'while adding this feature' task. Tests cover only the secondary task.
Base repo has no dmenu_provider.cpp or dmenu_provider.h, confirming these are new files added by the gold patch. But their existence is never verified by the test.

summary: The gold patch is comprehensive and correct, but the test is severely under-scoped. It only validates the config migration (moving launcher settings from shell.panel to shell.launcher) via a pre-existing roundtrip test with 3 changed field references. The entire DmenuProvider feature — which is the primary subject of the issue — is untested: no verification of config parsing for dmenu entries, command execution, line parsing, fuzzy filtering, activation logic, or provider registration. The test target doesn't even compile the DmenuProvider source files. A candidate that only restructures the config types and schema (without implementing DmenuProvider) would pass. Tests should be revised to cover DmenuEntryConfig TOML parsing, the DmenuProvider query/activate behavior, and ideally the application-level provider registration.
